title: Bad job interviews
paragraphs: Have you ever attended a job interview? For some people they can be a painful and embarrassing experience, but for others, it can be a chance to shine – a platform to perform and show off their talents. But sometimes, even for the most confident candidates, things don't go to plan and the interviewee is left feeling they'd wish they had never stepped foot in the room!

The interview is a necessary part of the recruitment process, and if carried out fairly, can be a good way to select the ideal person to fill a position in a company. This can be done by just asking questions or by carrying out other tasks that test someone's competencies. It's also a chance for the interviewee to ask questions and get a feel for their potential new employer. All this is to be expected when applying for a new job. But the BBC has found there are many examples of situations where inappropriate questions have been asked and irrelevant things have been discussed. Olivia Bland recently attended an interview at a technology company in the UK and claimed to have been subjected to a "brutal" two-hour job interview. She said the company's CEO "tried his best to intimidate" her and that in her feedback… "He told me everything I did was wrong, everything I said, the way I sat, my body language, everything that he could do to attack me." She actually got a job offer but turned it down. The CEO did apologise.

Other people have told the BBC about the grilling they received about their personal lives. For example, mature student Kevin Helton said "The interviewer asked, 'You used to be in the Army, how many people have you killed?'" Jo Foat was asked by an interviewer to wear a large straw hat and was told "In my experience, pretty girls like you rely too much on their looks."

There are, of course, laws against discrimination, and managers should only be asking questions that are relevant to a vacancy. But sometimes, according to James Reed, chairman of employment agency Reed, what may appear to be an inappropriate question is said "…to provoke you, and there's nothing illegal about provoking someone, but they can be annoying."

Of course, some unconventional job interviews can be fun and are designed to put you at ease. A French marketing agency is inviting applicants for an internship to discuss the opportunity over a game of Fortnite! Now that sounds like a fun way to develop your career!

vocabulary.entry: attend a job interview /əˈtend ə dʒɒb ˈɪntəvjuː/ 参加求职面试
vocabulary.example: She was nervous when she attended a job interview for the first time.
vocabulary.translation: 她第一次参加求职面试时很紧张。

vocabulary.entry: a chance to shine /ə tʃɑːns tu ʃaɪn/ 大放异彩的机会
vocabulary.example: The competition is a chance to shine for young musicians.
vocabulary.translation: 这场比赛对年轻音乐家来说是大放异彩的机会。

vocabulary.entry: show off one's talents /ʃəʊ ɒf wʌnz ˈtælənts/ 展示某人的才能
vocabulary.example: He used the performance to show off his talents in playing the piano.
vocabulary.translation: 他借着这场演出展示了自己的钢琴演奏才能。

vocabulary.entry: go to plan /ɡəʊ tu plæn/ 按计划进行
vocabulary.example: Unfortunately, the project did not go to plan due to funding issues.
vocabulary.translation: 遗憾的是，由于资金问题，项目未能按计划进行。

vocabulary.entry: step foot in /step fʊt ɪn/ 踏入；进入
vocabulary.example: He vowed never to step foot in that restaurant again after the bad service.
vocabulary.translation: 经历了糟糕的服务后，他发誓再也不踏进那家餐厅。

vocabulary.entry: recruitment process /rɪˈkruːtmənt ˈprəʊses/ 招聘流程
vocabulary.example: The company has simplified its recruitment process to attract more candidates.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司简化了招聘流程，以吸引更多求职者。

vocabulary.entry: fill a position /fɪl ə pəˈzɪʃn/ 填补岗位空缺
vocabulary.example: The manager is eager to fill the position with a qualified candidate.
vocabulary.translation: 经理急于找一位合格的候选人填补这个岗位空缺。

vocabulary.entry: test someone's competencies /test ˈsʌmwʌnz ˈkɒmpɪtənsɪz/ 测试某人的能力（复数）
vocabulary.example: The practical task is designed to test candidates' competencies in problem-solving.
vocabulary.translation: 这项实操任务是为了测试候选人的解决问题能力。

vocabulary.entry: get a feel for /ɡet ə fiːl fɔː/ 了解；熟悉
vocabulary.example: The internship allowed her to get a feel for the working environment of the company.
vocabulary.translation: 这次实习让她了解了这家公司的工作环境。

vocabulary.entry: inappropriate questions /ˌɪnəˈprəʊpriət ˈkwestʃənz/ 不当问题（复数）
vocabulary.example: Job seekers have the right to refuse to answer inappropriate questions in an interview.
vocabulary.translation: 求职者有权拒绝回答面试中的不当问题。

vocabulary.entry: be subjected to /bi səbˈdʒektɪd tu/ 遭受；经历
vocabulary.example: The workers claimed to be subjected to unfair treatment by the employer.
vocabulary.translation: 工人们声称遭受了雇主的不公平待遇。

vocabulary.entry: brutal /ˈbruːtl/ adj. 残酷的；严苛的
vocabulary.example: The team faced a brutal defeat in the final match.
vocabulary.translation: 这支队伍在决赛中遭遇了惨败。

vocabulary.entry: intimidate /ɪnˈtɪmɪdeɪt/ v. 恐吓；威胁
vocabulary.example: No one has the right to intimidate others in the workplace.
vocabulary.translation: 职场中没人有权恐吓他人。

vocabulary.entry: job offer /dʒɒb ˈɒfə(r)/ 录用通知
vocabulary.example: She was thrilled to receive a job offer from her dream company.
vocabulary.translation: 收到梦想公司的录用通知，她激动不已。

vocabulary.entry: turn down /tɜːn daʊn/ 拒绝
vocabulary.example: He had to turn down the invitation because of a prior engagement.
vocabulary.translation: 因为已有安排，他不得不拒绝这个邀请。

vocabulary.entry: grilling /ˈɡrɪlɪŋ/ n. 严厉盘问
vocabulary.example: The witness faced a grilling from the lawyer during the trial.
vocabulary.translation: 庭审中，证人遭到了律师的严厉盘问。

vocabulary.entry: discrimination /dɪˌskrɪmɪˈneɪʃn/ n. 歧视
vocabulary.example: The law prohibits discrimination based on gender, age or race.
vocabulary.translation: 法律禁止基于性别、年龄或种族的歧视。

vocabulary.entry: relevant to a vacancy /ˈreləvənt tu ə ˈveɪkənsi/ 与岗位空缺相关
vocabulary.example: Interview questions should be relevant to the vacancy to ensure fairness.
vocabulary.translation: 面试问题应与岗位空缺相关，以保证公平性。

vocabulary.entry: provoke /prəˈvəʊk/ v. 激怒；挑衅
vocabulary.example: His rude remarks were intended to provoke the other team members.
vocabulary.translation: 他的无礼言论是故意激怒其他队员的。

vocabulary.entry: unconventional /ˌʌnkənˈvenʃənl/ adj. 非常规的；非传统的
vocabulary.example: The artist is known for his unconventional painting style.
vocabulary.translation: 这位艺术家以其非常规的绘画风格而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: put someone at ease /pʊt ˈsʌmwʌn æt iːz/ 让某人放松
vocabulary.example: The interviewer's friendly smile put the candidate at ease.
vocabulary.translation: 面试官友好的微笑让求职者放松了下来。

vocabulary.entry: internship /ˈɪntɜːnʃɪp/ n. 实习岗位；实习期
vocabulary.example: She applied for an internship at the international company to gain work experience.
vocabulary.translation: 她申请了这家跨国公司的实习岗位，以积累工作经验。

sentences.english: Have you ever attended a job interview?
sentences.chinese: 你参加过求职面试吗？

sentences.chinese: 对一些人来说，面试是一段痛苦又尴尬的经历，但对另一些人而言，这是一个大放异彩的机会——一个展示才能的平台。

sentences.english: But sometimes, even for the most confident candidates, things don't go to plan and the interviewee is left feeling they'd wish they had never stepped foot in the room!
sentences.chinese: 不过有时候，即便是最自信的求职者，事情也可能不如预期，最后只希望自己当初没有踏进了那个房间。

sentences.english: The interview is a necessary part of the recruitment process, and if carried out fairly, can be a good way to select the ideal person to fill a position in a company.
sentences.chinese: 面试是招聘流程中必不可少的环节，如果能公平开展，它会是公司选拔岗位理想人选的有效方式。

sentences.english: This can be done by just asking questions or by carrying out other tasks that test someone's competencies.
sentences.chinese: 面试形式可以是提问，也可以是安排其他测试应聘者能力的任务。

sentences.english: It's also a chance for the interviewee to ask questions and get a feel for their potential new employer.
sentences.chinese: 这同时也是应聘者提问、了解未来雇主的机会。

sentences.english: All this is to be expected when applying for a new job.
sentences.chinese: 求职时遇到这些情况都在意料之中。

sentences.english: But the BBC has found there are many examples of situations where inappropriate questions have been asked and irrelevant things have been discussed.
sentences.chinese: 但英国广播公司发现，有很多面试存在提问不当、讨论无关内容的情况。

sentences.english: Olivia Bland recently attended an interview at a technology company in the UK and claimed to have been subjected to a "brutal" two-hour job interview.
sentences.chinese: 奥利维亚·布兰德近期参加了英国一家科技公司的面试，她称自己经历了一场“残酷”的两小时面试。

sentences.english: She said the company's CEO "tried his best to intimidate" her and that in her feedback… "He told me everything I did was wrong, everything I said, the way I sat, my body language, everything that he could do to attack me."
sentences.chinese: 她说公司首席执行官“想尽办法恐吓”她，并且在反馈意见中表示“我做的所有事、说的每句话、坐姿、肢体语言，他能挑刺的地方都攻击了一遍”。

sentences.english: She actually got a job offer but turned it down.
sentences.chinese: 她最终收到了录用通知，但还是拒绝了。

sentences.english: The CEO did apologise.
sentences.chinese: 这位首席执行官后来也道了歉。

sentences.english: Other people have told the BBC about the grilling they received about their personal lives.
sentences.chinese: 还有人向英国广播公司讲述了自己在面试中被追问私生活的经历。

sentences.english: For example, mature student Kevin Helton said "The interviewer asked, 'You used to be in the Army, how many people have you killed?'"
sentences.chinese: 比如成年学生凯文·赫尔顿说：“面试官问我‘你当过兵，杀过多少人？’”

sentences.english: Jo Foat was asked by an interviewer to wear a large straw hat and was told "In my experience, pretty girls like you rely too much on their looks."
sentences.chinese: 乔·福奥特则被面试官要求戴上一顶大草帽，对方还说“以我的经验来看，像你这样的漂亮女孩太依赖外貌了”。

sentences.english: There are, of course, laws against discrimination, and managers should only be asking questions that are relevant to a vacancy.
sentences.chinese: 当然，有反歧视相关法律规定，面试官只应提出与岗位相关的问题。

sentences.english: But sometimes, according to James Reed, chairman of employment agency Reed, what may appear to be an inappropriate question is said "…to provoke you, and there's nothing illegal about provoking someone, but they can be annoying."
sentences.chinese: 但招聘机构瑞德集团的董事长詹姆斯·瑞德表示，有时候一些看似不恰当的问题，其目的“是为了激怒你，激怒他人并不违法，但确实会让人不悦”。

sentences.english: Of course, some unconventional job interviews can be fun and are designed to put you at ease.
sentences.chinese: 当然，也有一些非常规的面试形式有趣又能让人放松。

sentences.english: A French marketing agency is inviting applicants for an internship to discuss the opportunity over a game of Fortnite!
sentences.chinese: 法国一家营销公司邀请实习申请者通过一起玩《堡垒之夜》来讨论工作机会！

sentences.english: Now that sounds like a fun way to develop your career!
sentences.chinese: 这听起来真是开启职业生涯的有趣方式。
